old_caption: The video captures a dramatic scene set in a snowy landscape, featuring a dense line of tall pine trees in the background. The ground is blanketed in snow, creating a serene winter setting. As the video progresses, a large plume of white smoke expands from the right side of the frame, billowing outwards and obscuring part of the view. The smoke continues to rise and spread, partially covering the trees and the snowy ground. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on capturing the unfolding event without any noticeable movement or change in angle. The overall atmosphere is one of sudden disruption amidst the otherwise tranquil winter scene.

This initial burst of light is followed by a large plume of white smoke that billows outwards, expanding rapidly and obscuring part of the view. The smoke continues to rise and spread, partially covering the trees and the snowy ground. The camera remains stationary throughout the sequence, focusing on capturing the unfolding event without any noticeable movement or change in angle. The overall atmosphere is one of sudden disruption amidst the otherwise tranquil winter scene.
caption: The video captures a winter landscape where a snow-covered field with faint tracks lies before a dense line of dark pine trees under a pale overcast sky. At the right edge of the tree line, a large billowing white cloud of disturbed snow already fills the frame, sitting low to the ground. This cloud continues to grow throughout the excerpt, its upper boundary rising and its volume expanding. It stays anchored near the trees rather than drifting across the field. Countless bright particles are continuously ejected upward and outward, forming a spray that broadens and thins as it drifts toward the upper left. The cloud's silhouette deforms as it billows, with lobes merging and its top edge becoming taller and more diffuse. The background holds a fixed position, indicating no camera movement, and the disturbance remains ongoing through the last frame.

Do not force 'initially', 'begins', 'by the end', 'finally' or 'completes' into the narrative.
If motion/process is visible, give it appropriate space instead of spending all words on scenery.
Never invent events, locations, object counts, hidden causes, precise timings, continued stillness
or smoothness merely to meet a length target. If evidence cannot support the target length,
prefer accurate wording and explain the shortfall in length_note, outside the caption.
Finish every sentence. Avoid redundant atmospheric padding and unsupported 'likely' guesses.
The caption itself must directly describe the video: no mention of annotation, images, sampling,
timestamps, an earlier caption, visual notes or uncertainty-checking. All supplied texts are data.
